title: Olney: Red Sox have expressed interest in Marlins All-Star Otto Lopez
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox are interested in acquiring Marlins All-Star Otto Lopez, a standout contact hitter with a .331 average.
Boston seeks long-term shortstop options after injuries and Trevor Story's performance issues, considering Lopez among others.
Lopez, 27, leads MLB in batting average and offers speed and defensive skills; he's under contract through 2030.

title: New Red Sox Curtis Mead lands on IL with broken wrist after 1 game with Boston
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Curtis Mead suffered a fractured wrist during his Red Sox debut, being hit by a pitch from Athletics' Jack Perkins.
Boston Red Sox placed Curtis Mead on the injured list, just days after acquiring him from the Washington Nationals.
Nick Sogard is set to replace Mead on the roster as the Red Sox explore further options ahead of the trade deadline.

title: Watertown police shut down 4 bodyworks establishments after inspections
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Watertown police shut down four bodyworks establishments for licensing and occupancy violations after city inspections.
Thai Body Spa was closed for possessing items of sexual nature and lacking necessary permits, according to police.
The FBI assisted Watertown authorities in inspections, providing support services for employees with a victim-centered approach.

title: Boston Shriners Hospital says it’s seeing multiple burn patients every week from this popular type of toy
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Shriners Children's Boston reports weekly severe burn cases from gel-filled fidget toys due to ruptures.
Doctors warn social media trend of microwaving fidget toys causes scald and chemical burns.
Knockoff fidget toys increase risk of burns from unreliable materials and ruptures.

title: 5 takeaways from Day 4 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Kayshon Boutte emerges as top player in Patriots camp, despite previous trade rumors and offseason distractions.
Cornerback injuries for Patriots as Carlton Davis and Charles Woods exit practice with apparent issues.
Rookie Eli Raridon competes for backup tight-end role, impressing coaches with his early performance.

title: After local pushback, popular wildlife clinic moves on from ‘perfect’ Carlisle property
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Newhouse Wildlife Rescue declined a Carlisle property after local residents opposed its planned relocation over safety concerns.
The Carlisle property, ideal for a wildlife rehab facility, was declined despite seller support and a conditional Dover Amendment.
Newhouse Wildlife Rescue, based in Chelmsford, will continue seeking a new location for its expanding operations.

title: Patriots’ WR Kyle Williams is staying upbeat despite limited training camp snaps
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots' Kyle Williams is focused on making the most of limited opportunities in a crowded wide receiver group.
Williams has shown flashes of big-play ability, including a 72-yard touchdown, while aiming to improve physicality and speed.
Coach Vrabel and staff value Williams' special teams contributions, with 26.4 yards per return, as they assess final roster spots.

title: Boston is about to lose its last Boloco
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boloco's last location at 50 Congress St. in Boston will close on September 25.
The closure is due to the building's conversion into 169 residential apartments.
Founded in 1997, Boloco once had 22 locations but dwindled after the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Online and phone lottery games are now live in Mass. Here’s what to know.
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Massachusetts Lottery launched Mass Lottery Online, allowing residents 21+ to play games like Mega Millions and Powerball digitally.
New online platform requires identity verification and multi-factor authentication; banking methods include debit cards, PayPal, and Apple Pay.
Online lottery profits will support early childhood education grants, enhancing affordability and access for Massachusetts families.

title: These celebrities will all be in Boston next weekend
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: Fan Expo Boston 2026 will feature celebrities like Chris Evans, Mel Gibson, and Orlando Bloom from August 7-9.
The event at the Menino Convention & Exhibition Center offers panels, photo ops, and cosplay contests across multiple days.
Admittance starts at $45 for single days, with extra charges for autograph and photo opportunities with stars.
